title: The Role of Microplastics in Marine Ecosystems

sections.heading: Reading Passage 1
sections.passage:
Microplastics, defined as plastic particles smaller than five millimeters, have become a pervasive pollutant in marine ecosystems. Research indicates that these tiny particles originate from various sources, including the breakdown of larger plastic debris, the shedding of synthetic fibers from clothing, and the use of microbeads in personal care products. Once released into the ocean, microplastics can be ingested by a range of marine organisms, from plankton to larger fish, leading to bioaccumulation throughout the food chain.

Recent studies highlight the potential impacts of microplastics on marine biodiversity. Organisms that ingest microplastics may experience physical harm, such as blockages in the digestive tract, as well as chemical exposure to harmful additives that are often present in plastics. Furthermore, these particles can absorb toxic substances from the surrounding water, which may then be transferred to predators when consumed. This introduces significant risks not only to marine life but also to human health, as seafood consumption is a common pathway for the transfer of these toxins.

Efforts to mitigate microplastic pollution are ongoing, with researchers advocating for improved waste management practices and the development of biodegradable alternatives to conventional plastics. Furthermore, public awareness campaigns are crucial in encouraging individuals to reduce their plastic footprint and support initiatives aimed at preserving marine environments. Without concerted action, the threat of microplastics to marine ecosystems is likely to exacerbate, necessitating urgent global attention and policy intervention.

questions.question: What is the primary concern about microplastics in marine ecosystems?
options: A) They are visible to the naked eye
B) They can harm marine organisms
C) They are easy to remove from the ocean

questions.question: Microplastics can absorb toxic substances from water.
